title: Redox Chemistry
seo_title: Secondary 4 Chemistry: Redox Chemistry Worksheets (O-Level 6092 with Answers)
standard_text: Define oxidation and reduction in terms of oxygen, hydrogen, electron transfer and changes in oxidation state; identify redox reactions, oxidising agents and reducing agents, including the use of acidified potassium manganate(VII) and potassium iodide; describe electrolysis of molten compounds and aqueous solutions using inert and copper electrodes, including selective discharge; describe electroplating and the purification of copper; describe simple cells and the hydrogen fuel cell (summary of the Singapore-Cambridge O-Level Chemistry 6092 syllabus).
meta_desc: Free Secondary 4 O-Level Chemistry worksheets on redox chemistry: oxidation and reduction, oxidation states, oxidising and reducing agents, electrolysis, electroplating, simple cells and fuel cells. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: OIL RIG: oxidation is loss, reduction is gain (of electrons).
key_sub: Cathode: cations reduced. Anode: anions oxidised.
body_html:
How to think about it

Oxidation and reduction always happen together.

  • Oxidation: gain of oxygen, loss of hydrogen, loss of electrons, increase in oxidation state. Reduction is the opposite.
  • The oxidising agent is reduced; the reducing agent is oxidised. KMnO₄ turns purple → colourless; KI turns colourless → brown.
  • Electrolysis: cations go to the cathode (reduced), anions to the anode (oxidised). In aqueous solutions of reactive metals hydrogen forms; dilute solutions give oxygen at the anode.
  • Simple cell: the more reactive metal is the negative terminal; further apart in the reactivity series gives a larger voltage.
Example

Oxidation state of S in H₂SO₄?

2(+1) + S + 4(−2) = 0

Answer: +6

Example

Electrolysis of dilute H₂SO₄ with carbon electrodes. Products?

cathode: H⁺ → H₂

anode: OH⁻ → O₂

Answer: hydrogen and oxygen (2 : 1 by volume)

Common mistakes

  • Saying oxidation is gain of electrons.
  • Saying the oxidising agent is oxidised.
  • Writing sodium at the cathode for aqueous sodium chloride.
  • Making the object to be plated the anode.

faq.q: How do you work out an oxidation state?
faq.a: Use the rules: oxygen is −2, hydrogen +1, Group 1 metals +1, and the oxidation states in a compound add up to zero (or to the charge of an ion).

faq.q: What decides the products of electrolysis of an aqueous solution?
faq.a: At the cathode, the less reactive of the metal and hydrogen is discharged. At the anode, oxygen forms from dilute solutions, but concentrated chloride or iodide gives chlorine or iodine; a copper anode dissolves.
The object is the cathode and the plating metal is the anode, in a solution of the plating metal's ions. Metal ions are reduced onto the object.
